words.tip: Soft 'ch'. Long 'aa' in the second syllable.
Final 'd' → 't'. 'Ik heb hoofdpijn' = I have a headache.
Plural: de vingers. 'Ik heb mijn vinger gesneden' = I cut my finger.
het-word, but the plural takes 'de': de oren. 'oorontsteking' = ear infection.
het-word → plural 'de ogen'. Soft 'g'. 'oogontsteking' = eye infection.
'eu' = the French 'eu' / German 'ö' sound. 'de neusspray' = nose spray.
Long 'ee' = 'ay'. 'Ik heb keelpijn' = I have a sore throat.
Short 'e'. The back/side of the neck (the front is 'de keel').
Short 'u', soft 'g'. 'Mijn rug doet pijn' = my back hurts.
'ui' vowel — the tricky one. 'buikpijn' = stomach ache.
Plural: de armen. Same as English.
het-word! Plural takes 'de': de benen. 'been' also means 'bone'.
'v' → 'f'. Plural: de voeten. 'te voet' = on foot.
Soft 'g' at the end. 'Hoest in je elleboog' = cough into your elbow.
Final 'd' → 't'. 'Was je handen' = wash your hands.
